```{r}
#| label: options

options(housepi.footer.warranty = TRUE)
```

A predictive check simulates household studies from the model and compares common household measures on them with the observed ones [@gelman_posterior_1996].
Before inference, the parameters are drawn from their prior: this is a prior predictive check, and it shows what the model and its priors expect to see.
After inference, the parameters are taken from the posterior draws: this is a posterior predictive check (PPC), and it shows whether the fitted model reproduces the data.
Both run through `check_predictive()`.
We use the same final-size example presented in [Get started](housepi.html):

```{r}
#| label: model-setup
library(housepi)
set_housepi_theme(colour_strips = TRUE)
set_housepi_summary(cri_level = 0.95)
set.seed(42)

hh_model <- flu_1918_frederick |>
  new_housepi_model("final-size") |>
  add_parameter(import = "template")
```

# Prior predictive checks

The template priors are uniform: on $[0, 1]$ for `alpha` and `beta`, on $[0, 3]$ for `gamma`.
Without posterior draws, `check_predictive()` draws `nrep` parameter sets from these priors and simulates one household study from each.
There are no draws to count, so `nrep` must be set:

```{r}
#| label: compute-prior-predictions
ppc_prior <- hh_model |>
  check_predictive(nrep = 200)
ppc_prior
```

Each measure stores the observed values next to the median and credible interval of the predictions.
For the attack rate by household size:

```{r}
#| label: prior-ar-plot
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Attack rates by household size comparing prior predictions (blue) and observed data (black points with sample sizes).
#|  Predicted values show median estimates with wide 95% credible intervals.
library(ggplot2)

col_dict_prior <- c(prior = "dodgerblue", observed = "black")

# extract values for attack rate
ggplot(ppc_prior$format_attack_rate(),
       aes(x = as.factor(hh_size), y = observed,
           label = sprintf("[%s]", counts))) +
  # prior predicted AR
  geom_point(aes(y = predicted, color = "prior")) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(y = predicted, ymin = cri_lower, ymax = cri_upper,
                    color = "prior")) +
  # observed AR
  geom_point(aes(color = "observed")) +
  # annotate observed counts
  geom_text(nudge_x = 0.3, color = col_dict_prior["observed"]) +
  scale_color_manual(values = col_dict_prior) +
  labs(x = "household size", y = "attack rate", color = "")
```

The prior intervals are wide and cover the observed rates: the priors allow the data without favoring it.
Their medians sit above most observed rates, as uniform priors on transmission put more weight on large outbreaks than these data show.
An observed value outside its prior interval would raise a warning to sign that the priors exclude what was observed and should be revised before inference. For example, with a too low community transmission rate we get

```{r}
#| label: warn-prior
ppc_prior_warn <- hh_model |>
  add_parameter("alpha", prior = "uniform", max = 0.01, append = TRUE) |>
  check_predictive(nrep = 200)
```

# Posterior predictive checks over cases distribution

We now run inference as in [Get started](housepi.html) and store the posterior draws:

```{r}
#| label: inference
hh_fit <- hh_model |>
  run_inference()
```

We can use the simulation process to challenge the validity of the inferred model on top of the original dataset.
We do so by computing the predicted distribution of household cases ("final size") per household size according to our posterior distribution (i.e. by producing simulations according to posterior values).

```{r}
#| label: compute-predictions
# compute posterior predictive checks
ppc <- hh_model |>
  # run simulations according to previous posterior traces in hh_fit
  check_predictive(hh_fit)
print(ppc)
```

To show both observed and predicted cases distributions by household size, we can extract the formatted table from our output object as follows.

```{r}
#| label: format-cases-distr
# for this part of the analysis we consider only house sizes up to 5
ppc$set_max_hh_size(5)

# return a data.frame with observed and predicted cases distributions
cases_df <- ppc$format_cases_distr()

# observed counts as they are, predictions with their credible interval
cells <- rbind(
  transform(cases_df, distribution = "observed",
            value = as.character(observed)),
  transform(cases_df, distribution = "predicted",
            value = format_credible_interval(predicted, cri_lower, cri_upper,
                                             as_integer = TRUE))
)

# one row per household size and distribution, one column per number of cases
# headers: "_" splits "number of cases" above the counts
combined <- cells[order(cells$hh_size), ] |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c("hh_size", "distribution"),
                     names_from = "cases", values_from = "value",
                     names_prefix = "number of cases_")
names(combined)[1] <- "size"

# generate cases distribution by household size table
ft <- flextable::flextable(combined) |>
  flextable::separate_header() |>
  flextable::bold(j = c("size", "distribution")) |>
  flextable::merge_v(j = "size") |>
  flextable::align(align = "center", part = "all") |>
  flextable::autofit()
# highlight the observed counts outside their credible interval
flagged <- cases_df[cases_df$outside, ]
for (k in seq_len(nrow(flagged))) {
  ft <- ft |>
    flextable::italic(i = which(combined$size == flagged$hh_size[k] &
                                  combined$distribution == "observed"),
                      j = paste0("number of cases_", flagged$cases[k]))
}
ft
```

Observed counts in italics fall outside the 95% credible interval of their prediction: these are the values flagged by `check_predictive()`.
The flags cover every household size, while the table stops at 5.
Bounds are rounded to integers, so an observed count equal to a printed bound can still fall just outside the unrounded interval.

# Secondary attack rate

We can compare the secondary attack rates observed, predicted by the posterior:

```{r}
#| label: sar-plot
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Secondary attack rates by household size comparing posterior predictions (orange) and observed data (black points with sample sizes).
#|  Predicted values show median estimates with 95% credible intervals.

# we remove the maximum house size before proceeding
ppc$set_max_hh_size(NULL)

col_dict <- c(posterior = "coral", observed = "black")
nudge_prior <- position_nudge(x = -0.25)

# extract values for secondary attack rate
ggplot(ppc$format_sec_attack_rate(),
       aes(x = as.factor(hh_size), y = observed,
           label = sprintf("[%s]", counts))) +
  # posterior predicted SAR
  geom_point(aes(y = predicted, color = "posterior")) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(y = predicted, ymin = cri_lower, ymax = cri_upper,
                    color = "posterior")) +
  # observed SAR
  geom_point(aes(color = "observed")) +
  # annotate observed counts
  geom_text(nudge_x = 0.3, color = col_dict["observed"]) +
  scale_color_manual(values = col_dict) +
  labs(x = "household size", y = "secondary attack rate", color = "")
```

# Other measures

`check_predictive()` also accepts named measure functions, computed on the simulated data and compared with the observed values.
They are checked alongside the standard epidemiological measures, so each needs a name of its own.
Current standard measures are stratified by household size:

- `measure_ar_by_hh_size`: attack rate;
- `measure_sar_by_hh_size`: secondary attack rate;
- `measure_cases_by_hh_size`: cases distribution.

`measure_geom_mean_hh_size` returns a single number instead: the geometric mean of household size weighted by secondary cases, a data-driven choice for `hh_size_ref`.

A custom measure function should accept a `data_wide` data.frame and return a `data.frame`, a `list`, or a `numeric` vector:
  
```{r}
#| label: predicted-measures-custom
# define a custom measure: overall attack rate
measure_overall_attack_rate <- function(data_wide) {
  sum(data_wide$status > 0, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(data_wide)
}

# compute standard and custom measures together
ppc_multi <- hh_model |>
  check_predictive(hh_fit, overall = measure_overall_attack_rate)
ppc_multi
```

The returned `HousepiEpiPredictiveCheck` object stores `observed`, `predicted`, `cri_lower` and `cri_upper` for each measure, accessible by name:
  
```{r}
#| label: extract-sar-components
# bind observed secondary attack rates
ppc_multi$sec_attack_rate$observed |>
  # to predicted (posterior mean) values
  dplyr::left_join(ppc_multi$sec_attack_rate$predicted, by = "hh_size",
                   suffix = c("_observed", "_predicted"))
```

With `epi = FALSE` only the custom measures are checked.
The result is then a `HousepiPredictiveCheck` object, without the formatted outputs and the household size bounds of the standard check:

```{r}
#| label: predicted-measures-only-custom
hh_model |>
  check_predictive(hh_fit, overall = measure_overall_attack_rate,
                   epi = FALSE)
```

Similarly can be done for all stored measures:

```{r}
#| label: plot-overall-attack-rate
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Overall attack rates comparison between observed and predicted.
#|  Predicted mean value shown with errorbars for the 95% credible interval
# compare observed vs predicted overall attack rate
ggplot(data.frame(ppc_multi$overall)) +
  geom_point(aes(x = "observed", y = observed), color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(x = "predicted", y = observed,
                    ymin = cri_lower, ymax = cri_upper)) +
  geom_point(aes(x = "predicted", y = predicted)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "attack rate")

```
